rationale: Paired with fire and pleasure (line 3) as a third dark element. Possibly ⲡⲉⲧ-ⲁⲟⲃⲉ where ⲁⲟⲃⲉ is a Lycopolitan form for an abominable/unclean thing. Etymology uncertain — possibly related to ϫⲁϩⲙ 'be defiled' or ⲁⲟⲩⲏⲃ 'slime, filth.' Confidence low; warrants comparison with K.30+.

Greek ζῴδιον 'small living figure' = zodiac sign. The 'twelve ⲍⲱⲇⲟⲛ of matter' = the twelve cosmic constellations as the dark frame of the visible cosmos. Standard Manichaean technical term for the zodiacal sphere of fate/matter.

Likely ⲣⲙ̄-ⲛ̄-ⲏⲥⲉ 'person of old/antiquity.' Hypostatized cosmic figure who 'reigns among the doctrines' and from whom the twelve zodiac-signs are manifest. Capitalized as a Manichaean cosmic title. Confidence low — could alternatively be ⲣⲙ̄ⲛ̄ϩⲏⲧ 'the prudent/wise one.'
Lycopolitan ordinal — possibly from ⲥⲁϣϥⲉ '7' via reduction, or ϥⲧⲟⲟⲩ '4'. Recurrent designation of a specific cosmic dwelling-place in this kephalaion's enumeration. Tentative.
Greek ζωγραφέω used as Coptic verb with prefix ⲣ̄- 'to do.' Cosmological term for the zodiac-signs as painters/depicters of the cosmic frame — the visible heavens as a painted projection from matter.
Already in vocab as 'doctrine' for philosophical schools. Here in cosmological register: the 'twelve doctrines' = the twelve cosmic teachings/laws that strip souls. Same lemma, theological extension.
